newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian unions threaten strike over failed deal.
newsitem.headline: Colombian unions threaten strike over failed deal.

text.p: Colombia's main unions have called a strike for May 28 to protest the government's failure to fulfill the terms of an accord that ended a week-long public sector strike in February, union officials said on Tuesday.

Julio Roberto Gomez, secretary general of the Democratic Workers' General Confederation (CGTD), the country's second largest labor federation, said no decision had been taken on whether the action would be indefinite or a 24-hour stoppage.
"In practice the government hasn't fulfilled any parts of the February accord. All the main unions have therefore agreed to strike on May 28," Gomez told Reuters.

The strike by an estimated 800,000 state workers in mid- February lasted a week before the government agreed to increase the average wage rise to 18 percent, compared with the weighted 13.5 percent rise it initially offered.

It also agreed to pass legislation granting all public sector workers the right to collective contract bargaining and to revise plans to restructure the public sector, which union leaders feared could lead to the loss of as many as 20,000 jobs.

Gomez said the main unions, to which most public sector workers are affiliated, would meet Thursday to discuss details of the strike. They were also due to meet with government ministers to find out why the accord had not been upheld.
